analysis: Integration pass over the full PR. All changes are CI-only runner sizing: .github/workflows/provider-plan.yml (comment block and lane table, head ~149-195) moves test lanes from 4x16/4x24 to 8x16 and GPU shard 2 to 12x32. The build lanes are unchanged. docs/developer/build.md gets a date bump, an interim-size paragraph and a table with a new 'Measured size' column. scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py replaces VALID_SIZES with PRODUCTION_SIZES={8x16,12x32} and remaps PLAN_LANES. A changelog.d entry describes the change and states 'No provider change'. The workflow, docs and test are consistent: every sized lane uses 8x16 or 12x32. No unit shows a change to workflow permissions, triggers, secrets, action pins or checkout. The route job's `permissions: {}` is unchanged. The tests still assert that the router accepts only exact labels, falls back on malformed grants, strips workflow-command injection from plane text, keeps release and credentialed workflows on literal runners (UNROUTED), and never contacts the plane for fork PRs. So the CI runner-selection trust boundary is not weakened. No provider runtime code, coordinator wire contract (TB-002), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-009, TB-011), key custody, add-on or GPU-limit boundaries (TB-012-014), or prefix-cache storage (T-041) are touched. No threat-model update is needed. Residual non-security notes: several shards (Runtime 2, Provider Unit Tests 2, GPU 1 and 3) run with less than the 1.25 memory margin on 16 GiB, so they may be flaky. That is an availability and test-quality matter that the docs state openly. The darkbloom-route.yml workflow file and the truncated parts of the patches were not supplied, so their consistency is unverified; the integration replay was also incomplete (15 units omitted). Neither point supports a security finding.
